gaps.text: Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Low-level fusion: MIR-ATR and fluorescence spectra from the same probe tip are synchronised and concatenated into one matrix with block scaling, since variables from different methods are not equivalent. Each instrument keeps its own calibration and diagnostics. The fused model must beat the best single method on held-out samples, otherwise the extra method is dropped.)

items.finding: Low-level data fusion rearranges data from different sources into a new matrix where variables are placed sequentially.
items.how_it_applies: This approach can be evaluated when combining multiple spectroscopic methods for tissue discrimination, provided the fused model is validated on independent samples.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited research focuses on food and chemical process matrices rather than in-vivo surgical tissue discrimination, so transferability to clinical environments remains uncertain.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
